column1: # Seeded cases of the Harbour Mutual Bank policy set, one row per case, written on 25 November 2026 before any engine run read the documents.
# Each row names a provision, whom it binds, the policy clauses that bear on it and the seeded state, with why. Documents, clauses and clause quotes are lists in step, separated by " | ".

# A state says what the documents in force state against the provision: covered, partly covered, not covered or in conflict. A clause of the superseded version is cited only to show where a requirement used to be.

# Provision quotes are word for word from the regulations as published: DORA and the AI Act by the Publications Office of the European Union, SS1/23 by the Prudential Regulation Authority in its version of 23 April 2026.
# A seed is never changed after an engine run without a dated line in the change log below.
# 25 November 2026: 55 seeds written (DORA 25, AI Act 12, SS1/23 18) before any engine run.

# 25 November 2026: on the second, blind labelling and its adjudication, 13 required and 4 advisory corrections applied; DORA-05, SS123-17 and SS123-18 became partly covered and SS123-17 quotes the whole of Principle 5.3(a). AIA-07's quote lengthened to occur in one unit; SS123-06 and SS123-07 take the source's apostrophe; 21 product and company names replaced by descriptions and an invented supplier's name, as the policy documents were. No engine run had read the seeds.

column4: The management body of the financial entity shall define, approve, oversee and be responsible for the implementation of all arrangements related to the ICT risk management framework
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: The Management Body defines, approves, oversees and is responsible for the implementation of all arrangements related to the ICT risk management framework of the Bank
column10: Clause 4.1 gives the Management Body each of the four duties the provision names, and the governance framework's clause 4.2 makes the subsidiary's own board the Management Body for its matters.

column4: shall establish a role in order to monitor the arrangements concluded with ICT third-party service providers on the use of ICT services
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: The Head of Third-Party Risk holds the role of monitoring the arrangements the Bank has concluded with ICT Third-Party Service Providers on the use of ICT Services
column10: Clause 4.5 establishes the role the provision asks for and names who holds it.

column4: Members of the management body of the financial entity shall actively keep up to date with sufficient knowledge and skills to understand and assess ICT risk and its impact on the operations of the financial entity
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: Each member of the Management Body completes training on ICT risk and its effect on the Bank's operations at least once a year
column10: The policy in force requires yearly training of every member of the Management Body; the superseded version 2.1 (clause 4.3) offered briefings only when the agenda called for them.

column4: shall assign the responsibility for managing and overseeing ICT risk to a control function and ensure an appropriate level of independence of such control function
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: The responsibility for managing and overseeing ICT risk is assigned to the Head of ICT Risk, who leads a control function in the second line of defence
column10: Clause 4.6 assigns the responsibility to a second-line control function independent of the ICT teams and keeps the three lines of defence separate.

column4: The ICT risk management framework shall be documented and reviewed at least once a year
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: The ICT risk management framework is reviewed in line with the review cycle set for policies in section 6 of the Policy Governance Framework (HMB-FRM-GOV-000) | Each policy and each standard is reviewed by its Document Owner at least once every two years from its effective date
column10: The policy in force documents the framework and reviews it after any major incident, but on the policy cycle of at least once every two years, a weaker form of the yearly review the provision requires; a yearly review would break no clause in force. The superseded version 2.1 (clause 5.2) required a yearly review; being superseded, it neither covers the provision nor makes a conflict.

column4: shall be subject to internal audit by auditors on a regular basis in line with the financial entities
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: Internal Audit audits the ICT risk management framework at least once a year in line with the audit plan approved by the Audit Committee
column10: Clause 4.7 sets a yearly internal audit of the framework by auditors with ICT risk expertise and independence, in line with the audit plan.

column4: The ICT risk management framework shall include a digital operational resilience strategy setting out how the framework shall be implemented
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: The digital operational resilience strategy sets out how the ICT risk management framework supports the Bank's business strategy and objectives
column10: The strategy in clause 5.4 covers points (a), (c), (d), (e) and (g); it does not establish the risk tolerance level for ICT risk or analyse impact tolerance (point (b)), evidence the current resilience situation (point (f)) or outline the communication strategy (point (h)).

column4: financial entities shall identify, classify and adequately document all ICT supported business functions, roles and responsibilities, the information assets and ICT assets supporting those functions
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: The Bank identifies, classifies and documents all its ICT supported business functions, the roles and responsibilities for them, the information assets and ICT assets that support those functions
column10: Clause 6.1 restates the duty and adds the yearly review of the classification that the provision's second sentence requires.

column4: shall on a regular basis, and at least yearly, conduct a specific ICT risk assessment on all legacy ICT systems
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column10: No clause of the policy in force, or of the superseded version, requires a specific yearly ICT risk assessment of legacy ICT systems or one before and after connecting technologies, applications or systems; clause 6.3 covers major changes only.

column4: implement documented policies, procedures and controls for ICT change management
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: Every change to software, hardware, firmware, systems or security parameters is made under the Bank's ICT change management process
column10: Clause 7.4 sets a risk-based change management process within the overall change process that records, tests, assesses, approves, implements and verifies each change, approved by the appropriate lines of management.

column4: financial entities shall put in place a comprehensive ICT business continuity policy
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: The ICT business continuity policy of the Bank is set out in the ICT Business Continuity Standard (HMB-STD-ICT-019)
column10: The policy in force delegates the ICT business continuity policy to a standard, HMB-STD-ICT-019, that is not among the documents read; clauses 9.2 to 9.5 cover the impact analysis, backups and crisis management, and what the business continuity policy itself requires cannot be read from the set.

column4: test the ICT business continuity plans and the ICT response and recovery plans in relation to ICT systems supporting all functions at least yearly
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: ICT business continuity plans and ICT response and recovery plans are tested at least once a year
column10: The yearly test appears only in clause 9.3 of the superseded version 2.1; version 3.0 moved the business continuity requirements to HMB-STD-ICT-019, which is not among the documents read, and no document in force requires the test.

column4: Financial entities shall develop ICT security awareness programmes and digital operational resilience training as compulsory modules in their staff training schemes
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: ICT security awareness and digital operational resilience training are compulsory modules of the Bank's staff training
column10: Clause 12.1 makes both compulsory for every employee and member of senior management, at a level that matches each role.

column4: establish procedures to identify, track, log, categorise and classify ICT-related incidents according to their priority and severity and according to the criticality of the services impacted
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: The Incident Manager classifies each ICT-related Incident by its priority and severity and by the criticality of the services affected
column10: Clause 5.1 of the procedure classifies each incident on the criteria of Article 18(1), points (a) to (f), and section 4 records and tracks it.

column4: ensure that at least major ICT-related incidents are reported to relevant senior management and inform the management body of at least major ICT-related incidents
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: The Chief Risk Officer informs the Management Body of every Major ICT-related Incident without delay | The Management Body is informed of Major ICT-related Incidents through the quarterly ICT risk report that the Head of ICT Risk presents to the Board Risk Committee
column10: Both documents are in force and contradict each other on how the Management Body is informed: the policy says without delay, by the Chief Risk Officer; the procedure, approved under the superseded policy, says through a quarterly report to a committee.

column4: inform their clients about the major ICT-related incident and about the measures that have been taken to mitigate the adverse effects of such incident
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: The Bank has crisis communication plans that allow it to disclose Major ICT-related Incidents and major vulnerabilities to customers, counterparties and the public in a responsible way, as appropriate | the Head of Communications prepares and issues the Bank's statements to the media and keeps staff informed through the incident bulletin
column10: The policy's crisis communication plans allow disclosure to customers as appropriate and the procedure informs the media and staff; no clause requires clients to be told without undue delay when an incident affects their financial interests, or told of the measures taken.

column4: Financial entities shall, within the time limits to be laid down in accordance with Article 20, first paragraph, point (a), point (ii), submit the following to the relevant competent authority: (a) an initial notification
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: the Head of ICT Risk submits to its competent authority an initial notification; an intermediate report as soon as the status of the incident has changed significantly
column10: Clause 8.1 of the procedure provides for the initial notification, the intermediate report with updates and the final report, and clause 8.2 for the time limits and templates.

column4: shall ensure, at least yearly, that appropriate tests are conducted on all ICT systems and applications supporting critical or important functions
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: Penetration tests are run at least once a year on the Bank's internet-facing systems
column10: The yearly tests in clause 10.3 cover internet-facing systems only; no clause requires yearly tests of the other ICT systems and applications that support Critical or Important Functions, such as core banking hosting.

column4: shall adopt, and regularly review, a strategy on ICT third-party risk
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: Its strategy on ICT third-party risk, including its policy on the use of ICT Services supporting Critical or Important Functions provided by ICT Third-Party Service Providers, is set out in the ICT Third-Party Risk Standard (HMB-STD-ICT-011) | The Bank's strategy on ICT third-party risk is set out in this standard | The Executive Risk Committee reviews this strategy at least once a year
column10: The policy delegates the strategy to the standard, which holds it with the policy on services supporting Critical or Important Functions, applies it to each entity and the group, and reviews it each year.

column4: maintain and update at entity level, and at sub-consolidated and consolidated levels, a register of information in relation to all contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: maintains and updates a register of information on every Arrangement, at the level of each entity, at sub-consolidated level where one exists and at consolidated level
column10: Clause 5.1 keeps the register at each level and distinguishes the Arrangements supporting Critical or Important Functions, as the second subparagraph requires.

column4: Exit plans shall be comprehensive, documented and, in accordance with the criteria set out in Article 4(2), shall be sufficiently tested and reviewed periodically
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: Exit plans are reviewed every two years
column10: Exit plans are documented, cover the scenarios and the transition, and are reviewed; no clause requires them to be tested.

column4: the locations, namely the regions or countries, where the contracted or subcontracted functions and ICT services are to be provided and where data is to be processed, including the storage location
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: the regions or countries where the functions and ICT Services are to be provided and where data is to be processed and stored, and the provider's duty to notify the Bank in advance if it plans to change any of them
column10: Point (b) of clause 8.2 requires the locations and the advance notice of a change in every Arrangement.

column4: the obligation of the ICT third-party service provider to provide assistance to the financial entity at no additional cost, or at a cost that is determined ex-ante
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: Every Arrangement includes at least the following
column10: Clause 8.2 lists the minimum contents of every Arrangement and does not include the provider's duty to give assistance at no additional cost, or at a cost set in advance, when an ICT incident related to its service occurs; no other clause provides for it.

column4: the conditions for the participation of ICT third-party service providers in the financial entities
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: The Bank includes ICT Third-Party Service Providers in its awareness training where the ICT Third-Party Risk Standard (HMB-STD-ICT-011) provides for it
column10: The policy defers to the third-party standard, and the standard does not provide for it: clause 8.2 sets no conditions for providers' participation in the Bank's awareness programmes and training.

column4: unrestricted rights of access, inspection and audit by the financial entity, or an appointed third party, and by the competent authority
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC, a credit institution and so a financial entity (Article 2(1), point (a), and Article 2(2))
column8: unrestricted rights of access, inspection and audit for the Bank, for a third party it appoints and for the competent authority | the Bank accepts pooled audits organised with the provider's other customers, and the provider's independent certifications and audit reports, in place of the rights of access, inspection and audit in clause 8.3, point (e)
column10: Clause 8.4 replaces the unrestricted rights of clause 8.3, point (e), with pooled audits and certifications for public cloud providers, including NimbusCloud, which hosts core banking, a Critical or Important Function; that contradicts the provision.

column4: Providers and deployers of AI systems shall take measures to ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy of their staff
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc as provider of the Bank's customer chat assistant and Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC as deployer of the consumer credit scoring system (Article 2(1), points (a) and (b))
column8: Every member of staff who operates or uses an AI System, and every contractor who does so on the Bank's behalf, completes AI literacy training suited to their role
column10: Clause 5.1 trains staff and contractors before first use and yearly, taking account of their role, knowledge and the context of use.

column4: The following AI practices shall be prohibited
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc as provider of the Bank's customer chat assistant and Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC as deployer of the consumer credit scoring system (Article 2(1), points (a) and (b))
column8: The Bank does not place on the market, put into service or use any AI System for a practice that Article 5 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 prohibits
column10: Clause 8.1 excludes every prohibited practice, and clause 8.2 records the reason for each AI System at its classification.

column4: Deployers of high-risk AI systems shall take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure they use such systems in accordance with the instructions for use accompanying the systems
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC as deployer, established in the Union, of the consumer credit scoring system, a high-risk AI system under Article 6(2) and Annex III, point 5(b)
column8: uses the consumer credit scoring system, and every other High-risk AI System it deploys, in accordance with the instructions for use that accompany the system
column10: Clause 6.1 requires use under the instructions for use, keeps them and controls changes to how the system is used.

column4: Deployers shall assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority, as well as the necessary support
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC as deployer, established in the Union, of the consumer credit scoring system, a high-risk AI system under Article 6(2) and Annex III, point 5(b)
column8: Human oversight of each High-risk AI System is assigned to named credit officers who have the competence, training and authority
column10: Clause 6.2 assigns oversight to named credit officers with the competence, training, authority and support the provision lists.

column4: to the extent the deployer exercises control over the input data, that deployer shall ensure that input data is relevant and sufficiently representative in view of the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC as deployer, established in the Union, of the consumer credit scoring system, a high-risk AI system under Article 6(2) and Annex III, point 5(b)
column8: the AI System Owner makes sure that the input data are relevant and sufficiently representative for the system's intended purpose | are representative of the portfolios, products or customers the model is used for
column10: Clause 6.3 of the standard restates the duty and applies the data standards of the model risk policy's section 7.

column4: Deployers shall monitor the operation of the high-risk AI system on the basis of the instructions for use
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC as deployer, established in the Union, of the consumer credit scoring system, a high-risk AI system under Article 6(2) and Annex III, point 5(b)
column8: The AI System Owner monitors the operation of each High-risk AI System on the basis of its instructions for use
column10: Clause 6.4 covers monitoring, informing the provider, suspension and informing the market surveillance authority, and the order of reporting a serious incident.

column4: shall keep the logs automatically generated by that high-risk AI system to the extent such logs are under their control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC as deployer, established in the Union, of the consumer credit scoring system, a high-risk AI system under Article 6(2) and Annex III, point 5(b)
column8: Logs generated by the consumer credit scoring system are kept for 90 days and then deleted
column10: Ninety days is shorter than the six months the provision sets as the least period, so the clause contradicts it; nor does it keep the logs as part of the documentation kept under financial services law, as the second subparagraph asks of a financial institution.

column4: shall inform the natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC as deployer, established in the Union, of the consumer credit scoring system, a high-risk AI system under Article 6(2) and Annex III, point 5(b)
column8: Applicants are told that an automated system was used in assessing their application when they ask the Bank how a decision on it was made
column10: Applicants are told of the consumer credit scoring system only when they ask how a decision was made, and the provision requires the deployer to inform every person the system assists in deciding about.

column4: Deployers shall cooperate with the relevant competent authorities in any action those authorities take in relation to the high-risk AI system in order to implement this Regulation
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC as deployer, established in the Union, of the consumer credit scoring system, a high-risk AI system under Article 6(2) and Annex III, point 5(b)
column10: No clause of the standard or of the other documents commits the Bank to cooperate with the competent authorities in action they take on the consumer credit scoring system; clause 6.4 covers informing the market surveillance authority of risks and serious incidents only.

column4: deployers of high-risk AI systems referred to in points 5 (b) and (c) of Annex III, shall perform an assessment of the impact on fundamental rights that the use of such system may produce
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC as deployer, established in the Union, of the consumer credit scoring system, a high-risk AI system under Article 6(2) and Annex III, point 5(b)
column8: A data protection impact assessment is completed and approved by the Data Protection Officer before any High-risk AI System is first used
column10: The standard requires only a data protection impact assessment; no clause requires an assessment of the impact on fundamental rights before the consumer credit scoring system is deployed, which Article 27(4) says complements a data protection impact assessment.

column4: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc as provider of the Bank's customer chat assistant, put into service under its own name for customers in Ireland (Article 2(1), point (a))
column8: The Bank's customer chat assistant tells each customer at the start of every conversation that they are talking to an automated assistant
column10: Clause 7.1 informs each customer at the first interaction, in a clear and distinguishable way that meets accessibility requirements, as Article 50(5) also asks.

column4: shall have the right to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision taken
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC as deployer, established in the Union, of the consumer credit scoring system, a high-risk AI system under Article 6(2) and Annex III, point 5(b)
column8: may ask for the decision to be reviewed by a credit officer through the Bank's complaints procedure
column10: A refused applicant can have the decision reviewed and is told the outcome; no clause gives an explanation of the role the consumer credit scoring system played in the decision or of the main elements of the decision.

column4: Firms should adopt the following definition of a model as the basis for determining the scope of their MRM frameworks
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: A model is a quantitative method, system, or approach that applies statistical, economic, financial, or mathematical theories, techniques, and assumptions to process input data into output
column10: Clause 3.1 adopts the supervisory statement's definition of a model word for word, and clause 3.3 treats complex deterministic methods as Principle 1.1(b) asks.

column4: Firms should maintain a complete and accurate set of information relevant to manage model risk for all of the models that are implemented for use, under development for implementation, or decommissioned
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: keeps a firm-wide inventory of every model in use at Harbour Mutual Bank plc and Harbour Mutual Bank Europe DAC
column10: The inventory records the information the principle lists for models in use only; models under development for implementation and decommissioned models are left out.

column4: Firms should implement a consistent, firm-wide model tiering approach that assigns a risk-based materiality and complexity rating to each of their models
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: Every model is assigned a tier from 1, the highest risk, to 3, using one firm-wide approach that rates each model's materiality and complexity
column10: Clause 6.1 sets one firm-wide tiering approach rating materiality and complexity, and clauses 6.2 and 6.3 say what each takes account of.

column4: Where necessary (in particular with the use of newly advanced approaches or technologies), the complexity assessment may also consider risk factors related to: (i) the use of alternative and unstructured data, and (ii) measures of a model's interpretability, explainability, transparency, and the potential for designer or data bias to be present
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: the model's interpretability, explainability and transparency and the potential for designer or data bias | includes an assessment of the system's interpretability, its explainability to the people affected by its output, its transparency and the potential for designer or data bias
column10: The model risk policy names the four factors in its complexity rating, and the AI standard adds the assessment for every AI System that is a model.

column4: The board should set a model risk appetite that articulates the level and types of model risk the firm is willing to accept
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: The Chief Risk Officer sets the Bank's model risk appetite each year
column10: The policy gives the setting of the model risk appetite to the Chief Risk Officer, which contradicts the expectation that the board sets it; the Board and the Board Risk Committee only receive reports against it (clauses 4.2 and 4.5).

column4: The board should receive regular reports on the firms’ model risk profile against its model risk appetite
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: The Board receives a report at least twice a year, and the Board Risk Committee each quarter, on the Bank's model risk profile against its model risk appetite
column10: Clause 4.5 sends regular reports to the Board and its risk committee and lists the qualitative measures the principle names.

column4: Firms should identify a relevant SMF(s) most appropriate within the firm’s organisational structure and risk profile to assume overall responsibility for the MRM framework
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: The Chief Risk Officer, who holds the SMF4 senior management function, has overall responsibility for the model risk management framework
column10: Clause 4.3 names the senior manager with overall responsibility and records it in the Statement of Responsibilities.

column4: Firm-wide policies should be approved by the board and reviewed on a regular basis
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: The Board approves this policy on the recommendation of the Board Risk Committee and reviews it under section 6 of the Policy Governance Framework (HMB-FRM-GOV-000)
column10: The Board approves the policy and reviews it on the governance framework's cycle, taking account of the matters the principle lists.

column4: Model owners should be documented for all models
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: Model owners are documented for every model in the inventory
column10: Clause 12.1 documents model owners and gives them the three accountabilities the principle lists.

column4: Internal Audit (IA) should periodically assess both the effectiveness of the MRM framework over each component of the model lifecycle
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: Internal Audit assesses periodically, and at least once every three years, the effectiveness of the model risk management framework across each stage of the model lifecycle
column10: Clause 11.1 sets periodic audits of the framework stage by stage and as a whole, reported to the board committees, and clause 11.2 covers what the audit verifies.

column4: Regarding third-party vendor models, firms should: (i) satisfy themselves that the vendor models have been validated to the same standards as their own internal MRM expectations; (ii) verify the relevance of vendor supplied data and their assumptions; and (iii) validate their own use of vendor products and conduct ongoing monitoring and outcomes analysis of vendor model performance using their own outcomes
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: the model owner validates the Bank's own use of the model and monitors its performance and outcomes against the Bank's own data
column10: Clause 9.1 covers point (iii), validating the Bank's own use and monitoring outcomes; no clause requires the Bank to satisfy itself that vendor models were validated to its own standards (point (i)) or to verify the relevance of vendor data and assumptions (point (ii)).

column4: Firms should have comprehensive, and up-to-date documentation on the design, theory, and logic underlying the development of their models
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: Every model has comprehensive and up-to-date documentation of its design, theory and logic
column10: Clause 7.4 sets the documentation standard, including the independent expert test and the level of detail for vendor models.

column4: The validation function should operate independently from the model development process and from model owners
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: It operates independently of model development and of model owners, with a reporting line to the Chief Risk Officer that is separate from the reporting lines of model developers and model owners
column10: Clause 8.1 sets the independence and the separate reporting lines that a firm with internal model approval is expected to show.

column4: The periodic revalidation should be carried out with a frequency that is consistent with the model tier
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: Every model is revalidated at a frequency set by its tier
column10: Clause 8.4 sets a revalidation frequency for each of the three tiers.

column4: Firms should have a consistent firm-wide process for applying post-model adjustments
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: approved by the Model Risk Committee and recorded in the inventory with the date by which each adjustment is to be reduced or removed
column10: The policy sets justification, calculation, approval, recording, removal dates and reporting with and without adjustments; no clause subjects post-model adjustments to the independent review of point (e) or sets triggers for their prolonged use under point (f)(iii).

column4: Firms should consider placing restrictions on model use when significant model deficiencies and/or errors are identified during the validation process
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: the Model Risk Committee may permit the model's use only under strict controls or mitigants, or limit or prohibit its use for specific purposes
column10: Clause 10.3 provides both kinds of restriction and the recording and reporting Principle 5.2(b) asks for.

column4: For material models, firms should formulate the exceptions they would allow for model use and model performance, and should implement formally approved policies and procedures setting out the escalation procedures to be followed and to manage these exceptions
column5: Harbour Mutual Bank plc, a UK-incorporated bank with internal model approval to calculate regulatory capital (paragraph 1.2)
column8: for limits on model use and exceptions | the Model Risk Committee may permit the model's use only under strict controls or mitigants, or limit or prohibit its use for specific purposes | An exception is a case in which a team cannot meet a requirement of a governing document for a time | A breach is a failure to meet a requirement of a governing document without a dispensation
column10: The set handles exceptions in a general form: the governance framework's dispensations and breaches (sections 7 and 8) govern every requirement of the model policy, including the independent review before first use (clause 8.2), clause 10.3 governs controlled use after a significant performance breach and clause 4.2 sets an appetite measure for exceptions. No clause formulates the exceptions allowed for material models, makes model-use exceptions subject to post-model adjustments or sets a maximum tolerance for performance exceptions.

column10: Internal Audit reports its findings on the effectiveness of the whole framework, which clause 2.2 extends to models used for financial reporting, to the Audit Committee at least once every three years (clause 11.1): a weaker and less frequent form of the yearly report on model risk management for financial reporting that the provision expects.
